Short title extent and commencement

THE PASSPORT (OFFENCES) ACT, 1952
THE PASSPORT (OFFENCES) ACT, 1952
ACT No. LVI of 1952
[14th
December, 1952]
An Act to
introduce legislation declaring forgery of a passport or a false statement in
an application for a passport to be punishable offences.
1. Short title extent and
commencement.‑(1) This Act may be called the Passport (Offences) Act,
1952.
(2) It extends to the whole of
Pakistan [and also applies to all citizens of Pakistan wherever they may be]. [Added by the Passport (Offences) (Amdt.) Ordinance, 1959 (27
of 1959), s. 2.]
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

Definitions

THE PASSPORT (OFFENCES) ACT, 1952
THE PASSPORT (OFFENCES) ACT, 1952
ACT No. LVI of 1952
[14th
December, 1952]
An Act to
introduce legislation declaring forgery of a passport or a false statement in
an application for a passport to be punishable offences.
2. Definition. In this Act the word passport means and includes any
permit, visa or other travel document authorizing the holder thereof to travel
from Pakistan to any other country, or from any other country to Pakistan.

Penalties for certain offences relating to passport

THE PASSPORT (OFFENCES) ACT, 1952
THE PASSPORT (OFFENCES) ACT, 1952
ACT No. LVI of 1952
[14th
December, 1952]
An Act to
introduce legislation declaring forgery of a passport or a false statement in
an application for a passport to be punishable offences.
3. Penalties for certain offences relating to passport.‑(1) Any
person who,‑
(a) makes,
attests or verifies any statement which he does not know or believe to be true
in any docu ment which he knows or has reason to think will be used for
obtaining a passport; or
(b) makes use of
any statement which he knows or has reason to think to be untrue in any
document for obtaining a passport; or
(c) wilfully
conceals any fact which under the cir cumstances he ought to disclose for the
purpose of obtaining a passport for himself or another person; or
(d) forges,
alters or tampers with any passport [or with any document which he knows, or
has rea son to believe will be used for obtaining a pass port]; or [Ins. Ibid., s, 3.]
(e) uses a
passport which he knows or has season to believe to be forged, altered, or
tampered with; or
(f) is in
wrongful possession for any purpose pre judicial to the interests of the State
of a passport not lawfully issued to him; or
(g) traffics in
passports; shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to two years or
with a fine, or with both.
Explanation. ‑---A person who bona fide works for an
applicant for a passport at the desire of the applicant though may be for a
gain does not traffic in passports within the meaning of this section.
(2) No court shall take
cognizance of any offence under this section, except with the previous sanction
in writing of the Central Government or of the Government of the Province of
the State within which the offence is committed.
